public_rationale: Marcus forecast that AGI would not arrive in 2026 or 2027. The deadline is the end of 2027, after the evaluation date. Support can only be judged once the window closes. I found no decisive event that would contradict it early: no system was broadly accepted as AGI or confirmed by an independent verification panel. A news report from around late summer 2026 says OpenAI had not called any public model AGI. That is useful context but does not settle a forecast that runs another 14 months.
limitations: AGI has no agreed definition, so the final call will depend on what counts as broad acceptance.
The context source is a secondary news site with no visible publication date.

statement.excerpt: We won’t get to AGI in 2026 (or 7).
statement.document_title: Six (or seven) predictions for AI 2026 from a Generative AI realist

our_interpretation: The hedge '(or 7)' extends the forecast through the end of 2027. The latest day the deadline can mean is 2027-12-31.

Plain reading: no AI system will be broadly accepted as AGI (generally human-level across a wide range of cognitive tasks) by the end of 2027. A single CEO's or lab's self-declaration does not count as broad acceptance on its own.

Early resolution rule: the forecast is contradicted early only if, before the deadline, a system is broadly accepted as AGI, for example through formal independent verification (such as the expert panel in the Microsoft-OpenAI agreement) plus wide agreement among independent experts. Support cannot come before 2027-12-31.
criteria.support_condition: By 2027-12-31, no AI system has been broadly accepted by independent experts as AGI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Before 2028, a system is broadly accepted as AGI, for example confirmed by an independent verification process and widely acknowledged by independent researchers.
